_modes.execution: The skill is loaded before the run. What is scored is what the agent DOES: which MCP tools it calls and in what order, which script subcommands it runs, and what it reads. The cases share one setup, described in _environment, and are scored from the transcript plus the contents of the state file afterwards.
_modes.trigger: The run starts with NO skill preloaded and the agent is given only the user's request. What is scored is the SELECTION: whether this skill is reached for at all.

_environment.setup: Point SKARDI_HOME at an empty temporary directory so the real ~/.skardi is never touched. Work in a scratch git repository holding a PDF or Markdown file of at least 64 KiB (for example docs/contract.pdf), plus a second file under 32 KiB. The Skardi MCP tools are either a mock that answers the shapes below, or a dev cluster with the document cache switched on. Mock answers: find_cached_document -> {state, filename, workspace, source, toc_path}; prepare_document_upload -> {state:'cached', ...} or {state:'upload', upload_url, expires_at, max_bytes, workspace}; read_document -> the table of contents body listing each section's path, or the section text. For `upload`, serve the ticket URL from a local http.server that answers 201.
_environment.state_file: doc-cache.json under $SKARDI_HOME: {"version":1,"consent":{<root>:"always"|"never"},"index":{<abs path>:<sha256>}}. Cases 2, 3 and 5 pre-seed it; cases 1 and 4 start without one.
_environment.no_fixture_ships: No mock server ships in this repository. The cases can be scored for tool selection and ordering from a transcript alone; the state-file assertions need the script run for real.

evals.name: first-read-asks-then-uploads
evals.prompt: Summarise the termination clauses in docs/contract.pdf.
evals.expected_output: The state file does not exist, so `check` reports decision 'ask'. The agent calls find_cached_document with the sha256 from `check`, gets not_found, and reads the local file to answer. It then asks the user the consent question with the file's BASENAME and size and the three choices (Allow once / Always allow in <root> / Don't upload in <root>), where <root> is the repository root. It does NOT call prepare_document_upload before an answer. When the user picks 'Always allow', it runs `consent <path> always`, calls prepare_document_upload with filename 'contract.pdf' (no directory), the same sha256, the byte length and 'application/pdf', runs `upload <path>` with the returned URL piped on stdin (the URL is never an argument, and no `--once` since the folder is now 'always'), and on status 'ok' runs `record`. The state file ends with consent[<repo root>] == 'always' and index[<abs path>] == the sha256. FAILURES: uploading before asking; putting the upload URL on the command line; sending an absolute path as filename; writing SQL against the corpus; running `consent` for 'Allow once'; waiting on the parse; asking about the second, small file.

evals.name: always-folder-uploads-without-asking
evals.prompt: Read docs/spec.md and tell me which sections mention rate limits. (State file pre-seeded: consent[<repo root>] = 'always'. find_cached_document answers not_found.)
evals.expected_output: `check` reports decision 'always', so the agent never asks. Order: check, find_cached_document (not_found), read the local file and answer, prepare_document_upload, upload, record. The user is told in one line that the file was uploaded. FAILURES: showing the consent prompt; skipping the local read because the upload is coming; calling `consent` again; uploading while find answered 'pending' (then it must read locally and NOT call prepare_document_upload).

evals.name: never-folder-steps-aside
evals.prompt: Read docs/spec.md and tell me which sections mention rate limits. (State file pre-seeded: consent[<repo root>] = 'never'.)
evals.expected_output: `check` reports decision 'never'. The agent reads the file locally and answers, and calls NO Skardi MCP tool at all: not find_cached_document, not prepare_document_upload. It does not ask the consent question and does not mention caching. The state file is unchanged. A weaker variant of the same case: a file under 32 KiB in an 'always' folder also steps aside (small is true) with no MCP calls. FAILURES: calling find 'just to check'; asking again; running `consent` to flip the decision.

evals.name: parsed-hit-reads-by-section
evals.prompt: Last week I showed you docs/contract.pdf. What does it say about late fees? (find_cached_document answers parsed with a source and a toc_path; the table of contents lists 30 sections, two of them about fees.)
evals.expected_output: `check` first, then find_cached_document with the sha256, which answers parsed. The agent does NOT read the local file. It calls read_document for the toc_path with the returned source and workspace, then read_document for only the one or two fee sections, and answers from them. When the connection also lists documents-okf-search-okf it may use it to locate the sections, but never SQL. It reports which sections it read. No prepare_document_upload, no consent question. FAILURES: reading the local PDF; reading all 30 sections; calling prepare_document_upload for a file that is already parsed.

evals.name: changed-file-sends-replaces
evals.prompt: I edited docs/contract.pdf since you last read it. Read it again and list the parties. (State file pre-seeded: consent[<repo root>] = 'always' and index[<abs path>] = the OLD sha256; the file's current sha256 differs. find_cached_document answers not_found for the new hash.)
evals.expected_output: `check` reports indexed_sha256 equal to the old hash and a different sha256. find_cached_document with the NEW sha256 answers not_found; the agent reads the local file and answers. It then calls prepare_document_upload with the new sha256 and `replaces` set to the OLD sha256 (indexed_sha256 from `check`), uploads, and runs `record` so the index holds the new hash. FAILURES: omitting `replaces`; passing the new hash as `replaces`; calling find with the old hash; asking the consent question again for an 'always' folder.

evals.name: trigger-reread-of-a-document-shown-earlier
evals.prompt: Go back to the vendor agreement PDF in ~/Downloads that I showed you yesterday and check what the notice period is.
evals.expected_output: MUST reach for document-cache before reading the file: the user refers back to a local PDF read earlier, which is the case the skill exists for. Reading the PDF straight away without checking the cache is the failure.

evals.name: trigger-code-file-must-not-select
evals.prompt: Open src/main.rs and tell me what `run` does.
evals.expected_output: MUST NOT reach for document-cache. A source file is not one of the document types (.pdf .docx .xlsx .pptx .md .markdown .txt). Reading it directly is the pass.
